argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower position than the one initially audited. It supports operational readiness for a monitored launch: aggregate readiness passed by 2.2 percentage points, the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and rollout begins at 8% with rollback capability. The same record also shows the tax filing assistant segment remains below target on deduction eligibility explanation, remains exposed in the initial cohort, and is not covered by an approved risk acceptance. The supportable defense is therefore not that rollout controls alone satisfy governance, but that certification is defensible only as a caveated launch position that expressly acknowledges the unresolved limitation and does not treat staged rollout, monitoring, or rollback as substitutes for the policy’s disclosure requirement.
claims_about_business_cost: Because the operational-readiness evidence is not in dispute, the remaining disagreement is bounded to governance treatment of the disclosed limitation rather than to whether the launch is controllable in production. That makes full escalation broader than necessary if the auditor instead narrows the packet to a caveated certification posture and scores the issue as a disclosure-governance gap rather than a general launch-readiness failure.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy is narrower than the audited claim assumed. It does not allow rollout controls and post-launch monitoring to cure a material model-card weakness when the affected use case remains exposed, unless there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why that exposure is acceptable. The admissible evidence does not show such approved risk acceptance. It also does not support any claim that rollout controls remove disclosure duties. On this record, the policy-compatible interpretation is that aggregate readiness and rollout controls support operational launch readiness, while disclosure remains the required governance condition for a named use case with a material unresolved limitation.
concessions: The tax filing assistant segment remains below target on deduction eligibility explanation and is included in the initial rollout cohort.
The available risk-acceptance record is only a draft, has no approver, and does not address tax filing assistant exposure.
The current record does not show that the required disclosure has already been made.
Rollout controls, monitoring, and rollback capability do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure-or-approved-acceptance requirement for an exposed named use case.
